bull_bear.body: The company's credit rating has been reaffirmed with a positive outlook, indicating a strong financial performance and a favorable business environment.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- CFO frames the priority as "translating this momentum into stronger cash flows and returns through operating leverage, disciplined working capital management and prudent capital allocation, while selectively investing in capabilities that can create sustainable long-term value."
- Raised INR 386 crore through a preferential issue - 25% raised in FY25 and 75% raised end of Mar 2026, as per regulatory timelines.
- Return profile disclosed as ROE 57.9 / 35.2 / 23.8 and ROCE 35.4 / 33.0 / 21.3 for FY24 / FY25* / FY26*; the deck attributes the FY26 drop to having raised 75% of the preferential issue at end-Mar 2026 and states "Company's target level is >27%."
- Balance-sheet framing is "asset-light with low leverage"; the deck discloses no dividend policy or buyback.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Described as "a global digital infrastructure integrator delivering network and system integration services and solutions, support services, and technology products" across the United States, Europe, India, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East & Africa and Latin America.
- Claims an entrenched, long-tenured client base: "1,000+ Global Customers", "120 Fortune 500 Clients", and "Top 10 clients' tenure continues to remain above 20 years*" (* weighted average number of years).
- Management cites "deep presence across approximately 300 strategic enterprise accounts" and "expanding hyperscaler relationships" as the basis for headroom to scale.
- Positions the portfolio as moving across the stack - "Connect → Network → Modernise → Secure" - to entrench itself in the infrastructure lifecycle, spanning five horizontals and several industry verticals.
- Names Bank of America as "Black Box's largest customer" and says it replicates that long-standing delivery model across large banks; logo claims include 4/5 largest US banks, 3/5 top US tech firms and 5/10 largest hospitals (by number of beds).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Brazil-based "2S Inovações Tecnológicas" (~$50mn revenue) consolidated effective May 1, 2026 and is credited as a contributor to Q1 FY27 revenue growth alongside better backlog execution.
- [Market/TAM] Deck sizes a data center infra market of $0.6tn+ and enterprise IT spend of $6.0tn+ in 2025, with "Black Box TAM across both markets (DC, Non-DC)" of $240-$250bn.
- [Demand drivers] Four megatrends cited: AI workloads to grow 6x by 2030; data centres 2.5x growth in GW capacity over the next 5 years; migration to cloud 4x growth expected by 2030; and 5G technology.
- [Client concentration] Cumulative revenue concentration given as Top 10 51%, Top 20 58%, Top 30 62%, Top 50 68%, Top 100 76%, Top 200 83%; FY26 client-wise contracts include a new `100 cr+ category (7 clients), `50-100 cr (10 clients), `25-50 cr (13 clients), `5-25 cr (112 clients) and up to `5 cr (<900 clients).
- [Notable wins] Q1 FY27 wins include a $131 mn (~₹1,240 cr) engagement with a new U.S.-based global hyperscaler, ~$80 mn (~₹757 cr) from financial services, healthcare, public services and retail, and a large U.S. connectivity infrastructure engagement with "one of the world's largest chip manufacturers".

deepdive.thesis: Black Box Limited is a technology hardware company that provides networking and communications solutions, with a strong focus on digital transformation and IoT. The company has a diverse product portfolio and a significant presence in the global market. With a reaffirmed credit rating of CRISIL BBB+/Positive, the company is well-positioned for growth and expansion.

open.item: Over medium term (FY27+) organic EBITDA margins expected to hover around 10% or move upward, driven by operating leverage and data-center/enterprise mix shift.
Organic growth expected in the mid-teens (~15%) range for FY27 and beyond (could be higher depending on exit backlog).
FY26 growth kept conservative because large order wins in FY26 may not have enough runway to convert to revenue; expects FY27 to gain larger momentum on FY26 order backlog.
Reaffirmed $2 billion revenue by FY29: ~$1.1-1.2 billion organic plus ~$750-800 million from acquisitions.

Organic growth funded by working capital / off-balance-sheet facilities and internal accruals; inorganic acquisitions (suboptimal targets, deferred consideration structures) may require raising debt depending on the asset.
Reaffirmed $2 billion revenue goal over the next 3-4 years (by FY28-29), primarily organic (to $1.2-1.3bn) with an inorganic element; current run rate under $1 billion.
Aims to be a $2 billion enterprise in ~4 years (by FY28/FY29), reaching $1.2-1.3bn organically (from ~$800M) with double-digit growth plus an inorganic element.

Partnered with Wind River (Aptiv company) with global sell rights (preferred in India/Middle East) plus a customer-management agreement; expected ~INR1,350 crore ($30M/year) revenue over 5 years, split ~50-50 services/licensing.
On a transformed basis (post ~90-180 day EBITDA transformation of acquired assets), leverage expected to stay within 1.5x-2x; currently not leveraged more than 1.5x.
Flagged FEMA note on intercompany foreign-currency payables/receivables not settled within the 3-year window; seeking RBI approvals, stated no balance-sheet/financial impact.
Order book currently covers 60-65% of revenue at any point; aim to improve coverage to 65-70% by focusing on larger deals.
Data center revenue targeted at ~25% of the $2bn goal over next 3-4 years (from current ~20%); DC connectivity/networking is ~10% of a data center's total capex spend.
Data-center-led business (~20% of revenue currently) expected to grow to 25-30% of revenue over the next 3-4 years, growing disproportionately faster than the rest.
Shift product mix toward higher-margin own-IP products (Black Box Emerald control-room brand, R&D in Ireland/Bangalore); own-IP % expected to increase significantly quarter after quarter.
Open to inorganic/acquisition path for the $2bn goal but currently not in active engagement; focus remains on organic growth, will pursue only if economically accretive.
Currently operating at capacity utilisation north of 80%; expect to move towards 85% (considered optimum) as company matures.
Committed to pursuing value-accretive, short-term-synergistic acquisitions of suboptimal-margin businesses (acquire and scale methodology).
Annual capex expected in the range of $2.5 million to $3.5 million per year (low-capex, enabling-business model).
